title: Adaptive Bitwidth Decision Lab - Console Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran an Optimize console walkthrough focusing on an adaptive bitwidth decision path for EverAid's clinical summarization workload. Demonstrated INT8 and FP8 profiles, live latency/throughput numbers, and rollback/fallback policies. Security questions were raised (KMS, audit logs, SOC2) and next steps include a sandbox pilot, a small benchmark run with customer prompt set, and delivery of pricing and security docs.
next_steps: SE to run 1k-sample bench with EverAid prompts and share CSV (due 2026-06-10)
AE to send pricing sheet for Dedicated and sandbox credits (due 2026-06-05)
Security doc pack (SOC2/KMS/Network) to be shared by Redwood (due 2026-06-04)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-03 16:00 PT | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Priya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros then we'll jump into the Optimize console and walk through an adaptive bitwidth decision path for your clinical summarization pipeline.
[00:12] Ellen: Thanks Priya. We're especially interested in keeping median tail latency under 300ms and ensuring summaries don't hallucinate more than 1-2% by our internal evals.
[00:20] Raj: Also want to understand what rollback looks like if FP8 shows a drift in clinical facts.
[00:27] Marcus (SE): Great, those are perfect constraints to validate. I'll share my screen and start in the Optimize tab, show existing q-profiles, then run a small live sampling against a canned prompt set. Apologies if audio is a bit rough — connection's fuzzy.
[00:42] [screen share starts] Marcus: Alright, this is the Optimize console home, we've got a set of q-profiles — you can see default-int8-speed, conservative-fp8, and a hybrid-adaptive profile we built for latency-first workloads.
[01:05] Raj: Can you explain the hybrid one? Is it a run-time switch based on token budget?
[01:10] Marcus: Yeah, hybrid-adaptive uses a small decision matrix: short responses (<64 tokens) route to INT8 fast path; mid-length (64-256) try FP8 with sampling, and long responses fallback to FP16 or a higher precision variant if the KV cache hits are low. The console allows threshold tuning and canary rules for rollout.
[01:29] Ellen: Interesting. How intrusive is that for our infra — do we need to change model artifacts?
[01:34] Marcus: No artifacts changes. These are runtime profiles — compiled kernels are selected based on the profile. For private deployments we recommend shipping the q-profiles as a config that you can pin.
[01:45] Tom (SRE): Quick security question — will the decision logic touch our data plane or is it all in the control plane?
[01:51] Ana (Product): Decision logic executes in the serving runtime on the inference node; no decisions are sent to Redwood control plane. Audit logs of which profile was used are emitted to your log sink if you enable that.
[02:03] Sofia (Security): And KMS? We need to ensure keys never leave our VPC and HSM usage for model artifacts.
[02:09] Marcus: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for Private deployment; for Hosted we have envelope encryption and SOC2 compliance documentation which we'll share after.
[02:21] [02:21] Marcus: Okay, demo time. I'm switching to the sandbox project named 'EverAid-demo'. First, baseline: FP16 resident model — 1920 sequence length, serve single-worker — median token latency ~48ms, end-to-end summary latency for typical prompts ~420ms.
[02:40] Raj: Those numbers are inline with our expectation for FP16. What gains do we see for INT8?
[02:44] Marcus: INT8 fast path — after quantization and kernel tuning — shows about 2.6x throughput improvement and median per-token latency down to ~18ms in this shape, bringing end-to-end down to ~180-220ms depending on prompt. Quality impact measured on your short clinical NER/summarization set — Rouge-L change is ~-1.8% mean, entity recall dip of ~2.2% on average.
[03:08] Ellen: That's promising. What about FP8? We've heard FP8 can be better than INT8 for some models.
[03:13] Marcus: FP8 conservative profile typically gives 1.9x throughput vs FP16 and a smaller quality delta: Rouge-L -0.8% and entity recall -0.7% in our sample. But FP8's sensitivity can vary by layer; some runs show slight stability issues so we recommend a narrow rollout.
[03:30] Raj: How do you detect drift or degradation in production?
[03:33] Marcus: Two parts — telemetry: we sample outputs (configurable sampling rate) and run lightweight automated checks like entity-fidelity, hallucination heuristics, and token-level perplexity jump detection. Second, you can configure automatic rollback rules — e.g., if entity recall drops by >1% on sampled traffic for 30min, switch to fallback profile (fp16 or int8-safe).
[03:50] Ellen: Can we see that in the console?
[03:52] Marcus: Yep, I'm toggling to the 'Rollouts' view. Here you can set canary percentages, monitoring hooks (your eval set or live sampling), and fallback policies per model version. We also include a heatmap view of quality vs latency so you can pick an operating point.
[04:10] [04:10] Priya: Quick callout — pricing impact. For INT8 we estimate unit token cost reduction roughly 45-55% vs FP16 on similar hardware due to higher throughput and amortization. FP8 sits between at ~30-40% savings but with slightly higher monitoring overhead. We'll send a pricing calc later.
[04:27] Tom: On dedicated — if we reserve capacity, does Redwood enforce the same kernels? We don't want surprise kernel swaps on update.
[04:33] Marcus: For Dedicated you can freeze kernel versions and we support the 'pinned-runtime' option so behavior won't change without a controlled deploy. Private gives you even more control.
[04:43] Raj: Can we run a targeted bench here? Maybe 1k prompts sampled from our production logs with our stop-conditions?
[04:49] Marcus: Yes — that's part of the sandbox engagement. We'll run INT8, FP8 conservative, and hybrid-adaptive, capturing latency distributions and automated quality scores. Expect a CSV with per-example metrics.
[04:59] Ellen: What's the expected Hallucination delta for FP8 worst-case? You mentioned sensitivity earlier.
[05:03] Marcus: In an aggressor run where we stress edge-case prompts, we saw an incremental hallucination rate up to +3.5% relative to FP16 in one outlier model family. That's why we recommend the narrow canary first and the automated rollback threshold. For many model+workload combos it's under +1%.
[05:23] Raj: If we do a canary and see destabilization, how fast is rollback?
[05:27] Marcus: Rollback is immediate at the routing layer; it flips traffic within seconds from the profile registry. The serving nodes will run the fallback kernels for subsequent requests.
[05:36] [05:36] Marcus: I'm going to run a quick live sample: 5 prompts from your anonymized prompt set. First run: baseline FP16, second: INT8, third: FP8 conservative.
[05:48] [06:00] FP16 run — output appears, latency 430ms end-to-end, entities preserved.
[06:08] Marcus: Now INT8 — latency 210ms, note one truncated medical acronym got slightly botched in the summary, we flagged it in the automated quality check.
[06:20] Raj: That's the kind of edge-case we care about — abbreviations and lab values.
[06:24] Marcus: FP8 run next — latency 300ms, quality close to FP16; no truncated acronyms this sample, but small changes in punctuation.
[06:36] Ellen: That aligns with the perf-quality curve we want. Can you show how to configure thresholds for switching?
[06:41] Marcus: Back to Rollouts > Thresholds. Here you can set a rule: if 'entity_recall_delta' < -1% for >5m, then reduce canary to 0 and send an alert, and optionally create a support ticket. You can set sampling windows and minimum sample count.
[06:58] Priya: For SLA language, customers typically ask for median P95 latency targets. We can vendor SLA on Dedicated with credits for regression. We'll put proposed SLA terms in the package.
[07:09] Tom: How do we store the sampled outputs? We need them in our S3 with encryption and retention policy.
[07:14] Ana: The sandbox can write sampling outputs to your S3 via configured sink; they're subject to your retention and KMS policies. For Hosted we can push to your log forwarder.
[07:25] Sofia: On compliance — can you share SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary?
[07:29] Priya: Yes — we'll share the pack after the call. Also we have an architecture doc for Private with HSM details.
[07:37] Raj: Any limitations for very short completion sizes? A lot of our summarization is 16-32 tokens.
[07:42] Marcus: For ultra-short outputs INT8 can be fantastic — sometimes you see 3-4x per-token improvements. But the decision policy here routes short responses to the fast INT8 path by default. FP8 doesn't add much benefit for tiny outputs.
[07:56] Ellen: What about long-running sessions where KV cache grows — any perf cliffs?
[08:00] Marcus: Cache size and architecture matter; we instrument KV cache hits in runtime and the console shows expected throughput vs sequence length. For very long sequences, the kernel selection prefers FP16 to avoid cumulative quantization error.
[08:13] Raj: Can you tag runs with our tenant id for debugging?
[08:16] Marcus: Yes, sampling payloads include tenant id and request id; logs are emitted with correlation ids.
[08:22] [08:22] Marcus: Now switching to the 'Heatmap' view — this is a visual tradeoff: x-axis latency, y-axis quality delta, each point is a profile. You can hover to see per-token medians and cost delta.
[08:36] Ellen: Nice. I'd like a CSV export of that chart for our cost modeling.
[08:40] Marcus: Exported. I'll include that in the bench artifact.
[08:44] Priya: Quick note on hardware: INT8 gains were measured on A100-like GPUs with INT8-optimized kernels; on older GPUs the improvement is smaller. We'll include hardware recommendations.
[08:58] Raj: For Private on-prem, we run Ampere GPU clusters but older firmware — how sensitive is the kernel compatibility?
[09:03] Marcus: There's a compatibility matrix; small kernel patches may be needed. For on-prem we provide the runtime package and test harness.
[09:12] [09:12] Ellen: Okay, question from Product side — how are user-facing rollouts coordinated across versions? If we change the model, do the profiles automatically reassess?
[09:19] Ana: Profiles are per model version. When a new model version is deployed, Optimize will run compatibility checks and optionally run a trial sample before promoting the profile to production. Manual approval gates exist.
[09:30] Tom: Any known issues with token streaming and hybrid-adaptive? Some of our UI expects partial tokens.
[09:36] Marcus: Streaming is supported; the runtime ensures compatible streaming semantics. When mid-response profile switches are necessary we buffer until the switch point; it's seamless for downstream consumers. There's a small extra latency on mid-response switches which the console reports.
[09:51] Raj: I'm worried about telemetry noise — for medical texts minor punctuation changes shouldn't trigger rollbacks. How fine-grained are checks?
[09:58] Marcus: You can select fidelity metrics — entity-level only, semantic-similarity thresholds, or custom redaction-safe checks. We usually recommend entity-based checks for clinical workloads.
[10:10] Ellen: Great. Let's talk about the hybrid-adaptive strategy — we'd prefer conservative defaults then gradually open it.
[10:16] Marcus: That's what the canary tooling is for. I can set a rule: start at 1% traffic for 24 hours, evaluate metrics, then 5%, then 20. Also a safety window: if any connected metric crosses the threshold it auto-reverts.
[10:29] Priya: We'll also provide a runbook: sample rate suggestion, guard rails, and a rollback playbook.
[10:35] Sofia: For legal, we need agreement language about model changes and data retention during sampling. Who owns the sampled data?
[10:41] Priya: Sampled outputs are owned by you; Redwood only processes them per the contract and deletes hosted copies per retention policy unless you opt-in to share them for model improvements.
[10:53] Raj: Can we get an estimate for the cost delta if we run hybrid-adaptive at steady state 50% INT8, 30% FP8, 20% FP16?
[11:00] Marcus: Rough ballpark: relative to FP16 baseline cost 1.0, blended unit cost ~0.62 — depends on throughput shaping and occupancy. We'll provide a spreadsheet with assumptions.
[11:11] Ellen: Any hard requirements for the initial sandbox? We can provide 1k prompts, access to a test S3 bucket, and a non-prod VPC if needed.
[11:17] Marcus: That's perfect. For private test we'll need access details for KMS or a test key; for hosted sandbox we'll need the prompt CSV and a sample eval set.
[11:27] [11:27] Marcus: Running a second live stress test — long prompt, 1.8k tokens. FP16 baseline: 2.4s, INT8 path aborted early due to quant noise, FP8 stable at 1.3s. This shows long-tail sensitivity — the policy sent long responses to FP16 in our hybrid-adaptive configuration.
[11:46] Raj: Okay that makes sense. For long prompts we may accept higher latency.
[11:50] Marcus: We recommend defining SLO buckets by prompt length. Console can map traffic into buckets and apply separate profiles.
[11:58] Ellen: Anything else for compliance? Audit logs need to be immutable and time-stamped — can Redwood deliver that?
[12:03] Ana: Yes, we support export to your WORM-compliant store and can integrate with SIEM via log streaming.
[12:10] Priya: Time check — we're about 12 minutes in, and it's been a productive run. Quick recap and action items, then open Q&A.
[12:17] [12:17] Priya: Recap: we'll run the 1k bench (Marcus), share pricing (Priya), send SOC2 + KMS docs (Priya), and Ana will prepare the console q-profile runbook. Customer to share compliance sheet (Sofia/Tom).
[12:31] Ellen: Sounds good. A couple of quick clarifications — what is your recommended sampling rate for production?
[12:36] Marcus: For high-risk clinical workloads start at 3-5% sampling with stratified sampling across request types and then reduce to 1% after stability is proven.
[12:45] Raj: And if noise causes false positives in the first week, can we widen thresholds instead of immediate rollback?
[12:51] Marcus: Yes — you can have an 'escalate' state: instead of rollback, widen thresholds or reduce canary from 5% to 2% while you investigate.
[12:58] Sofia: Last question — data residency: any EU-only processing options for PHI?
[13:03] Priya: Private deployment in EU regions is supported; we can propose a Private or Dedicated topology with EU-only data paths.
[13:11] Ellen: Great. Let's wrap. Thanks everyone.
[13:15] [End of meeting summary and recording stop]

Notes about transcript: occasional speech recognition errors (e.g., "fp eight" as "fp ate"), some speaker labels generic. The console screenshots were shared via the meeting chat as links: https://redwood.example/share/everaid-qprofile-heatmap, https://redwood.example/share/everaid-bench-csv
